title: Amores Perros
events_chronological: Octavio shares a cramped Mexico City house with his mother, his brother Ramiro, Ramiro's wife Susana and their baby.
Ramiro robs a pharmacy by night and beats Susana at home, and Octavio begins pressing her to run away with him.
Octavio discovers that Ramiro's rottweiler Cofi kills other dogs on sight and starts entering him in the local dogfights, winning steadily.
Octavio pays two thugs to beat Ramiro, who responds by taking Susana, the baby and Octavio's hidden savings and disappearing.
Model Valeria Amaya's lover Daniel walks out on his wife and daughters and moves her into a new apartment facing her own billboard.
In a last fight the promoter Jarocho shoots Cofi in the ring, Octavio stabs him and flees with his friend Jorge.
Octavio runs a red light at speed and ploughs into Valeria's car.
El Chivo, a former guerrilla turned vagrant contract killer, is at the junction and drags the bleeding Cofi out of the wreck.
Valeria wakes in hospital with her leg pinned together and her lapdog Richi lost somewhere in the new apartment.
Richi falls through a hole in the floorboards, and Daniel tears up the floor while Valeria's leg turns gangrenous.
Valeria's leg is amputated and the billboard carrying her image is taken down.
Ramiro is shot dead robbing a bank, and at the funeral Susana refuses Octavio's last offer to leave with him.
El Chivo nurses Cofi back to health among his own pack of strays.
The businessman Gustavo hires El Chivo to murder his half-brother and business partner Luis.
El Chivo watches from a distance as his estranged wife is buried, then follows his grown daughter Maru home.
Cofi kills every other dog in El Chivo's yard while he is out, and El Chivo puts a gun to the dog's head and cannot fire.
El Chivo abducts Luis but chains him up in his lair instead of killing him.
El Chivo brings Gustavo face to face with his brother, leaves a loaded pistol between them, and walks out having taken money from both.
El Chivo breaks into Maru's flat, leaves a long confession of who he is on her answering machine and takes her photograph.
Shaved and in clean clothes, El Chivo leaves his money for Maru and walks out into the wasteland with Cofi.
syuzhet_notes: The film opens on the crash (told-order bullet 1) and then restarts three times, telling three stories that overlap around it. The Octavio chapter runs up to the crash, the Valeria chapter begins before it and continues past it, and the El Chivo chapter takes it in stride at told-order bullet 14. Because the strands are largely simultaneous rather than consecutive, strict chronology interleaves bullets the film keeps in separate blocks.
fabula_notes: The three chapters overlap in time, so the placement of the Valeria and El Chivo material relative to the Octavio material is inferred from the shared crash rather than stated on screen. Ramiro's fatal bank robbery happens off screen and is only reported at his funeral.
